title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
lede: TechCrunch is keeping a running list of AI products and startups that shut down, pivoted or fell short, spanning consumer apps, hardware and features inside the largest companies.

points: Character.ai filed for bankruptcy in early October after lawsuits and regulatory pressure; Disney opened bidding at $20 million for a license to some of its IP.
OpenAI reversed a cluttered July ChatGPT redesign, discontinued its Atlas browser and shut down Sora in March 2026.
Apple's delayed Siri overhaul contributed to a $250 million settlement before reaching English-language users this month.
Relay, Notion Mail and Huxe closed as bigger platforms, or users' own agents, took over what they did.
S&P Global estimates that about 42% of corporate AI initiatives end up abandoned.

sections.text: Several of these closures came from a platform absorbing a stand-alone product's core feature, a risk worth weighing for anyone building thin tools on top of the large model providers.
